transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03 17:30 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Carlos Martinez (Head of ML - BrightHealth), Emily Chen (Eng Manager), Aisha Khan (Senior SWE)

Summary (auto-generated): quick SDK walkthrough for Python and TypeScript, auth setup, env var patterns, and next steps for pairing and security docs.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, i have Priya here the systems engineer, we'll do a quick SDK walkthrough for python and type script, show the quickstarts, how to wire auth, and cover common enterprise questions.
00:12 Carlos: Thanks, Jordan. Quick context — we're evaluating a LLM inference provider to power our clinical summarization pipeline. Primary concerns are privacy (PHI), latency under 600ms for short contexts, and cost. We're leaning toward hosted if encryption and auditability are solid, otherwise private.
00:30 Priya: Got it, that aligns with what Jordan told me. We'll show the SDK workflows, and then cover our Private and Dedicated offerings and the KMS options.
00:45 Emily: And Aisha will be the one doing the integration so we might ask her to pair.
00:52 Aisha: Yep, happy to pair after this.
01:05 Jordan: Alright, quick agenda: pip/npm install, setting REDWOOD_API_KEY in env, minimal python example, typescript example with streaming, and tips for testing in staging + canary rollouts.
01:18 Priya: One note, the SDK names are redwood-client for both languages, we have an official python package and an npm package. sometimes the package name in our docs shows an old internal alias, so use the link I'll send.
01:35 Jordan: Ok first, auth. You set a per-environment API key in env vars, e.g., export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-prod-xxxx for linux/mac, or set it in your CI secret store for pipelines. For Private/VPC customers we also support mutual TLS and customer-managed KMS for key wrapping.
01:55 Carlos: So for PHI, we'd want customer-managed keys and an on-prem or VPC deployment — is that right?
02:03 Priya: Yes, that's the common pattern. Private (VPC) gives you control over networking and can integrate with your KMS/HSM for at-rest key material. We also have audit logs and token-level tracing in the Console.
02:18 Aisha: If we use Hosted but with KMS, does Redwood manage the key or do we?
02:24 Priya: Hosted can integrate with your cloud KMS via brought-your-own-key (BYOK) for certain enterprise plans, but for full isolation you'd want Private. We'll add the exact matrix in the follow-up notes.
02:40 Jordan: Now the python quickstart — simple snippet:
02:45 Speaker 2: "from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv(\"REDWOOD_API_KEY\"))
resp = client.generate(model=\"redwood-8k-v1\", prompt=\"Summarize the following note...\")
print(resp.text)"
03:05 Aisha: Wait, is generate synchronous? How do you handle streaming?
03:10 Priya: Good question. We provide both a convenience sync generate and a streaming method. For streaming you do client.stream_generate(... ) and hook into chunk callbacks or use the SSE/websocket approach in the SDK. In python there is a simple iterator pattern. We'll paste examples.
03:28 Jordan: For TypeScript the pattern is similar — install @redwood/client, and then:
03:34 Speaker 1: "import Redwood from '@redwood/client'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const stream = client.stream.generate({ model: 'redwood-8k-v1', prompt: '...' })
stream.on('data', chunk => { /* append to UI */ })
stream.on('end', () => { /* finalize */ })"
03:55 Emily: For our web UI we'd want to do streaming to show partial results. Are there CORS or browser key leakage concerns we should be aware of?
04:04 Priya: We recommend routing through your backend for browser apps to avoid exposing keys. For sample apps we show a proxy pattern and short-lived session tokens — you can mint ephemeral tokens from your backend with restricted scopes.
04:20 Carlos: Does the SDK support role-scoped tokens or RBAC?
04:25 Priya: We have per-key scopes and the Console supports RBAC configs per team. We'll share a screenshot from the Console in the follow up.
04:35 Jordan: Quick note on environment setup: recommend per-env keys (dev/stage/prod). In CI set secrets and use canary routes in the Console for safe rollouts. For large-batch jobs use our deduped-batching endpoint — we'll send perf settings.
04:53 Aisha: On the code side, any gotchas for dependencies or python versions?
04:58 Priya: Python 3.9+ recommended; the SDK pins some http libs. For TypeScript node 16+ is fine. For serverless deployments prefer the streaming websocket approach to avoid cold-start token overhead.
05:12 Jordan: Example quickstart file locations: github.com/redwood/integrations/quickstarts/python and /typescript. I'll send those links.
05:22 Emily: Great. Now about model selection — we want predictability and small variance in latency. How do you recommend balancing model size and quantization?
05:35 Priya: For latency-critical workloads you can use smaller model variants or quantized releases; Redwood Optimize provides quantization profiles and suggests model/quantization per workload. We can run a small benchmark with your sample payloads.
05:50 Carlos: Are these quantized models available in Hosted?
05:54 Priya: Yes, many quantized variants are available in Hosted. Dedicated also supports custom quantization and kernel tuning, and Private allows you to bring custom artifacts.
06:06 Aisha: If we need custom tokens per-patient, can we pre-cache KV for prefixes? Will that hurt throughput?
06:13 Priya: We support prefix/KV caching. It speeds up repeated contexts but you need to tune batch sizes — Optimize will recommend batching and cache policies to hit your latency SLOs.
06:25 Jordan: Security questions — SOC 2, SSO, audit logs. We have SOC2 Type II, SSO via SAML/OIDC, and audit logs with export. For Private, we can restrict egress and provide on-prem packages. Priya will share the security pack.
06:45 Carlos: Good, please send SOC2 report and data handling docs.
06:50 Priya: Will do.
06:54 Jordan: Ok, demoing a small live Python run — I'm going to paste a tiny note through the quickstart; you may see some transcription oddities in the live demo.
07:05 Speaker 2: ">>> sample prompt submitted... response stream starts... 'Patient presents with cough and low fever, recommended follow-up chest x-ray'..."
07:20 Aisha: Looks good. Latency on that small prompt was about 220ms for us in staging, which is promising.
07:28 Priya: Nice, that fits your 600ms target with headroom. For larger context (8k) we need to check throughput. We'll run the perf test.
07:40 Jordan: On billing — hosted is usage-based per token and embeddings, Dedicated has reserved capacity, Private is licensing + infra. We'll send a pricing sheet.
07:52 Carlos: Do you have volume discounts for committed reserved capacity?
07:56 Jordan: Yes, Dedicated has commit tiers. We'll include baseline numbers in the follow-up.
08:04 Emily: A few practical questions — logging: can we get full request/response logs or are they redacted?
08:12 Priya: Audit logs are redacted by default for PHI but you can opt-in for more verbose logging in Private/with contract and proper controls. We'll add docs.
08:23 Aisha: For on-call debugging, is there a way to replay requests against a pinned model?
08:28 Priya: Yes, the Console supports replaying a request against a pinned model version in a sandbox. That's useful for regression checks.
08:38 Jordan: Wrap up — recap of next steps: Jordan sends quickstart links and pricing; Priya sends security pack and perf spreadsheet; schedule pairing session for next week for python integration with Aisha.
08:50 Carlos: Great, thanks. Anything else?
08:53 Emily: Just to confirm, can you include a sample CI workflow for running integration tests against a staging key?
08:59 Jordan: Yes, we'll include a sample GitHub Actions snippet.
09:05 Aisha: If we want to run an internal benchmark, what's the best artifact to share?
09:10 Priya: Share a small corpus of anonymized prompts and expected token lengths and target p99 latency. We'll take it and run throughput/latency tests and send numbers.
09:20 Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items mentioned.
